answer: Plants use gravity to orient themselves, a process called gravitropism. Their cells, particularly those in the root and shoot tip, have statocytes with starch grains that help sense gravity direction. In roots, gravity pulls these grains to the bottom, triggering a redistribution of auxin hormones that promote growth and direction, leading the root to grow downwards, towards gravity. This helps roots reach water and nutrients, while shoots grow against gravity.
